newsitem.title: MEXICO: FORECAST-Femsa Q1 seen strong, but beer sales flat.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Femsa Q1 seen strong, but beer sales flat.

text.p: Weaker beer volumes should take the shine off otherwise bright first quarter results for Mexican brewer and bottler Fomento Economico Mexicano SA (FEMSA), analysts said.
FEMSA impressed analysts with a buoyant fourth quarter of last year, keeping operating costs down and outpacing No. 1 brewer Grupo Modelo SA in sales volume growth by 7.2 percent to 6.6 percent.

The down side for the first quarter is expected to be flat to slightly lower beer sales volumes domestically compared with the first quarter of 1996 -- largely attributed to a weak recovery in consumer demand.
Beer exports, led by the Sol brand, are seen rising 10 percent to 15 percent.
Apart from its main beer division known as Cerveceria Cuauhtemoc Moctezuma, FEMSA has interests in soft drinks, owns the Oxxo chain of convenience stores and has its own packaging division.

Coca-Cola FEMSA SA, an affiliate that bottles and distributes the famous soft drink in Mexico and Argentina, came out of recent doldrums to post an 11.9 percent profit margin in the fourth quarter, a trend seen continuing.
Coca-Cola FEMSA accounts for about 30 percent of FEMSA's sales.
Strong results from Coca-Cola FEMSA, which appears to be gaining market share on Pepsi distributor Grupo Embotellador de Mexico SA de CV, Gemex, will help offset flat beer sales, analysts said.
Here are the results of a Reuters survey of three analysts, with 1996 figures adjusted up 24.5 percent for inflation:

Analyst Scott Weiss of D.A. Campbell in Los Angeles said streamlining has boosted FEMSA's profitability per hectoliter of beer, and the company recently took a bold step forward by implementing a new, decentralized distribution setup that gives regional managers more clout.
"They're getting a much better feel for the demands," Weiss said.
FEMSA spent much of 1996 improving its debt picture, shifting debt from the holding level down to the subsidiaries.
The debt picture improved this week when FEMSA announced at a shareholders' meeting that it had secured a $350 million syndicated loan to replace a $300 million Eurobond that comes due on July 22.
"It's definitely being well-received," Greg Rianhard, an analyst with Interacciones in Mexico City, told Reuters.
((--Dan Trotta, Mexico City newsroom, +525 728-9507))
